We currently sample it for fat and protein analysis and would like earlier information about composition changes. Product temperature and texture vary during production. We want an initial spectroscopy concept and a practical comparison experiment, while retaining our laboratory checks.

assessment.status_reason: One customer premise is contradicted by the sources: that the method can handle varying temperature and texture. A source warns that the reflection signal is sensitive to surface characteristics and fat globule size, and that calibration is specific to the matrix and its physical variation; the effect of temperature variation is not addressed at all. That premise underlies the request for earlier in-line composition information, so the honest status is premise_not_supported rather than a provisional method choice. The shortlist below is therefore offered as conditional hypotheses to test: it applies only if the physical state at the measurement point can be stabilised, or if the texture/temperature variation is deliberately covered in the calibration set and the model re-validated on that material. No performance figure (accuracy, detection limit, response time, fiber length) is claimed for this product; those remain unknown and are asked for.

recommendations.rationale: An opaque, concentrated milk product matches the documented dairy precedent for inline NIR reflection; NIR penetrates up to several millimetres and suits remote fiber-probe measurement; fat and protein are quantified in dairy by PLS regression on reflection data. Single method to test first.
recommendations.conditions: Applies if the probe can be mounted at a point with adequate contact/backscatter and if the product is not so optically thick that the reflected signal is unusable.

citations.quote: Inline NIR Reflection is primarily used for opaque or highly concentrated dairy products, such as yogurt, butter, or whole milk concentrates.

using Partial Least Squares (PLS) regression to quantify fat and protein

recommendations.rationale: MIR ATR passes in-line screening and is listed as a dairy technique for chemical/structural information that NIR might miss; MIR shows well-defined bands, and in a tissue study the fat-related ester carbonyl C=O band and the protein amide I/II bands are used. Keep it as a single-method comparison against the best single method.
recommendations.conditions: Applies only if the product allows tight contact with the ATR crystal (liquid or soft solid) and if crystal fouling/cleaning is manageable.

citations.quote: advanced labs often incorporate Fluorescence, Raman, and Mid-Infrared (MIR) ATR fiber optic techniques to capture specific chemical or structural information that NIR might miss.

the stretching vibration band of the ester carbonyl C=O at about 1740 cm-1
the amide I and II bands, two major absorption peaks of the protein peptide group in the infrared region
suitability of analyzed samples for ATR measurements, which is true for liquid or soft solid samples and their components, allowing a tight contact with the probe head.

recommendations.rationale: Conditional on the optical state at the measurement point. recommendations.conditions: Applies only if a suitable point exists and a defined pathlength (order 1-10 mm) can be maintained; otherwise not applicable.

measurement_concept.probe_and_geometry: In-line insertion probe at one defined point on the processing line, with the spectrometer remotely connected by fiber. Probe type, mounting and fiber link depend on the chosen point (pressure, flow, cleaning, distance).
